768c333a-82d4-4605-9aed-bbbf6c9ab311.title: Marlowe — Geographically Accurate Cartography
768c333a-82d4-4605-9aed-bbbf6c9ab311.visualDirection: branch off Editorial Motion v2, NOT yet selected (kept as a reversible alternative): the Schengen exchange section's donut chart is replaced with an interactive editorial-style Western Europe map (UK/Ireland/France/Iberia/Italy) — pulsing dots at 5 sample past-trip cities (London/Paris/Milan/Lisbon/Faro), dashed amber flight-arc lines from London (hub) to each, hover reveals a boarding-pass/trip-detail card; always-visible '61 of 90 days' summary stays for no-hover legibility. v1-v3 attempts (AI-hand-drawn SVG paths from a text prompt, even with a reference image) all produced unrecognizable blob shapes — LLMs cannot reliably vectorize/trace real geography from a prompt. v4 fixes this deterministically: built outside the AI generator using real Natural Earth land data (world-atlas npm package) through d3-geo (Mercator projection, clipped to a Western Europe bounding box), city dot positions computed from real lat/lon coordinates, then spliced into the draft HTML and imported via `import-design-draft --into`. Verified in-browser (Chrome) before import: real coastlines, correct city placement, working hover tooltips. This is the same stack the production plan calls for (@bklit/choropleth-chart also uses d3-geo + real geo data), so the mockup and the eventual React implementation now agree on approach.
